binge-watching = watching many episodes of a series one after another
subscription = a regular payment that gives access to a service or publication
mass media = newspapers, television, radio and large websites that reach huge audiences
public service broadcasting = radio and television funded to inform, educate and entertain, not only to profit
listed building = a historic building legally protected from harmful alteration
folklore = the traditional stories, songs, customs and beliefs of a community
high culture = art forms traditionally seen as serious and elite, such as opera and classical music
popular culture = entertainment and fashions enjoyed by large numbers of ordinary people
cultural heritage = the buildings, objects, traditions and knowledge inherited from the past
artefact = an object made by people in the past, of historical interest
UNESCO World Heritage Site = a place recognised internationally as having outstanding cultural or natural value
cultural identity = the sense of belonging to a group that shares language, traditions or history
cultural appropriation = adopting elements of a minority culture in a way many see as disrespectful or exploitative
censorship = official control that forbids or cuts parts of books, films or news
copyright = the legal right to control how a work is copied, performed or sold
intellectual property = legal rights over creations of the mind, such as books, films, designs and inventions
fair dealing = limited legal use of copyrighted material, for example for criticism or teaching
patron of the arts = a person or organisation that gives money to support artists or cultural institutions
commercialisation of culture = turning art and traditions mainly into products to sell
spin = presenting information so that it looks better than it is
